card: This pull request fixes a C++ One Definition Rule (ODR) violation in benchmark code and enables LTO in Alpine CI to catch future ODR violations. Two benchmark files defined conflicting `InputType` enums in the global namespace, triggering GCC `-Wodr` warnings under LTO. The fix wraps the benchmark enums in anonymous namespaces and enables `CMAKE_INTERPROCEDURAL_OPTIMIZATION` on Alpine Linux CI. It is a low-risk developer tooling and test fix.
evidence: PR description quotes the compiler failure: `/ci_container_base/src/bench/bip352.cpp:22:12: error: type ‘InputType’ violates the C++ One Definition Rule [-Werror=odr]`.
problem: Both `bench/bip352.cpp` and `bench/sign_transaction.cpp` defined global `enum class InputType` with different values, causing an ODR violation during link-time optimization. Additionally, CI did not build with GCC LTO, allowing such ODR violations to slip through unnoticed.

risk.why: A mistake would only affect benchmark compilation or increase Alpine CI build times.

summary: This pull request places the `InputType` enum class definitions in `src/bench/bip352.cpp` and `src/bench/sign_transaction.cpp` inside anonymous namespaces to resolve a C++ One Definition Rule (ODR) violation. It also enables interprocedural optimization (LTO) in the Alpine CI job so GCC can detect future ODR violations via `-Wodr`.
